input.library.name: Library files
input.library.description: Every video in the libraries that use this workflow.

ignore.description: Folders, files or patterns in the library that are left out.
ignore.title: Exclude patterns

filter.video_skips.name: Leave some files alone
filter.video_skips.description: Skips Dolby Vision files, files already in this format, and AV1 or VP9 videos.

includeDolbyVision.description: Off: Dolby Vision files are left as they are. On: they become HDR10 and the Dolby Vision layer is removed. Some Dolby Vision files (profile 5) are always left alone, because converting them would show wrong colours.
includeDolbyVision.title: Include Dolby Vision files

video.convert.name: Convert video
video.convert.description: Makes the video smaller at the quality you choose.

format.title: Video format
x-enumHints: Small files that play on most TVs and phones made since 2016.
Plays on everything, even old devices. Files are much larger than HEVC.
The smallest files, but slow to make and only for newer TVs and devices.
Small files for web browsers and Android. Few TVs play it.

maxBitrate.description: Caps how much data each second of video may use. A file never gets more than it has now. Quality still sets the picture; the cap only matters in busy scenes.
maxBitrate.title: Max bitrate

vbrMaxKbps.description: No scene goes above this. The picture aims for Balanced quality (CRF 23).
vbrMaxKbps.title: Max bitrate

quality.title: Quality
x-enumHints: The smallest files. Fine detail can soften, mostly in dark or busy scenes.
Small files, with a small loss of fine detail.
Little visible change for most people. A good start.
Keeps more detail. Files stay larger.
Hard to tell from the original. Files stay largest.

resolution.description: Videos are only ever made smaller, never stretched.
resolution.title: Resolution

speed.description: Slower takes about twice as long.
speed.title: Speed

audio.tracks.name: Audio
audio.tracks.description: Which sound tracks the new file has.

audio.title: Audio
x-enumHints: Plays on every TV and phone. Surround sound becomes stereo.
Adds a stereo track for phones and TVs, and keeps the original surround track for sound systems.
The best surround sound for modern TVs and sound bars.
Surround sound that plays on almost every TV and sound bar; older than E-AC-3.
The smallest audio, for MKV files. Doesn't play on Apple TV or most TVs.
Tracks are copied unchanged.
x-enumLabels: Stereo AAC, plus surround as it is

onlyMyLanguages.description: Keeps only tracks in your languages (Settings > General). Tracks with no language set are always kept. If none match, a stereo choice keeps the main track; the other choices keep all tracks.
onlyMyLanguages.title: Only my languages

subtitles.tracks.name: Subtitles
subtitles.tracks.description: Which subtitles the new file keeps.

subtitles.description: Subtitle pictures are never burned into the video.
subtitles.title: Subtitles
x-enumHints: Every subtitle track is kept as it is.
Keeps subtitles in your languages (Settings > General) and those with no language set; the others are left out, even if none match.
Picture subtitles are left out. Text subtitles are kept.
Text subtitles are saved next to the new file as .srt files instead of inside it; picture subtitles stay inside the file.

fileType.title: File type
x-enumHints: Holds every kind of track; the usual choice for Plex and Jellyfin.

Best for phones, browsers and Apple TV. Files with picture subtitles are left alone (the reason is in Jobs) unless the Subtitles step leaves those out. Styled subtitles become plain text. Surround formats MP4 can't hold become E-AC-3.
For web browsers. Only with AV1 or VP9 video and Opus audio.
Each file keeps its current type. A file whose type can't hold the chosen video or audio becomes MKV.

verify.output.name: Check the result
verify.output.description: The new file must play through, look like the original and hold what you chose. If not, the original stays.

output.commit.name: Save the result
output.commit.description: Where the new file goes, and what happens to the original.

folder.description: New files go to this folder, in the same sub-folders.
folder.title: Folder

folderMode.description: Pick a folder next to each library, or one folder for all of them. Your originals stay where they are.
folderMode.title: Where new files go
x-enumHints: Each library gets a folder beside it, e.g. /media/movies (shrunk). Same disk, and it works when one workflow serves several libraries.
Every converted file goes into the folder below, in the same sub-folders as in its library.

policy.title: Save the result
x-enumHints: New files go to the folder below, in the same sub-folders. Your originals aren't changed, so no space is freed until you remove them yourself.
The original is kept for 7 days (Settings > Safety), then deleted. This frees space. You can get an original back from its job.
Both stay. Nothing is deleted.
x-enumLabels: Put the new file next to the original

video.legacy_settings.name: Earlier install's settings
video.legacy_settings.description: The settings this workflow had before workflows existed. They run exactly as before; to change them, start from the Shrink videos steps.
